messages:
alex: Noticed a reproducible stale-read after prefix eviction in staging. Read returned value from an older epoch for ~300ms. Repro attached below.

jing: Oof. Can you paste the logs/seq ids?

alex: Logs: 
```
[evict-coordinator] dispatch(evict prefix=org:88:user, epoch=204) -> target shard-3
[shard-3] apply-evict(epoch=204) -> removed entries
[shard-3] evict-ack -> evict-coordinator (ack lost?)
[worker-12] cache-hit(prefix=org:88:user, epoch=203) -> served stale value
```

sophie: Sounds like workers didn't observe the epoch bump. Are we relying only on the sequencer to broadcast epoch/tombstones?

alex: Current flow: evict-coordinator -> RPC to primary shard to remove entries; coordinator also writes an async tombstone event to sequencer. Workers subscribe to sequencer and treat sequencer epoch as canonical. There's a window where RPC completed but sequencer event not yet processed by a worker.

ravi: Right. That window lets a worker serve the cached entry if it uses a local fast-path without validating with the shard/sequencer.

jing: Brainstorm options: 
- force synchronous broadcast to all local workers (correct but will hurt p99)
- keep a monotonic per-prefix metadata token and validate on cached hits (cheap in steady state)
- attach a per-request lease/ownership check (strong but adds RTT complexity)
- accept weak visibility and add soft-ttl after evict (worse correctness)

alex: I like the per-prefix token idea as a middle ground. Sketch: store a 64-bit token per prefix in shard metadata. On eviction, coordinator increments token and evicts local entries. Workers keep a tiny in-memory token cache for prefixes. Each cached KV line carries the token it saw on insert. On Get: if cached.token < current_token -> synchronously revalidate with shard (or wait for sequencer event). If cached.token == current_token -> serve locally.

sophie: That avoids blocking all reads on every eviction and keeps the check O(1) in the common case. Tradeoffs: the metadata tokens are extra memory and metadata store becomes a hot spot for super-hot prefixes.

ravi: We can co-locate the token store with shard metadata to avoid cross-shard requests. Also, keep the worker token cache TTL very small (e.g., 100ms) to cap the chances of stale reads.

jing: Implementation notes: token bumps are monotonic ints. Eviction flow: bump token in shard metadata store, publish tombstone to sequencer (best-effort), evict local entries. On Get miss or token mismatch, perform a CAS-like read against shard metadata to confirm token and either refresh or return miss.

alex: Edge cases: what if token increment write fails but evict RPC succeeds? We'll need a failure mode where the coordinator retries token bump before declaring eviction complete. For Dedicated deployments we might require sync guarantees; for Hosted we could accept token eventuality with strict monitoring.

sophie: Test plan: add a synthetic harness that does: write -> evict -> immediate read from different worker with artificial sequencer lag. Run many iterations to measure stale-read probability. Also add a canary in staging that simulates sequencer lag and asserts stale_reads < threshold.

prefetch-bot: EvictionReproTests queued (id=8172).

jing: Another micro-optimization: piggyback token in existing RPCs (e.g., model responses) so workers can opportunistically learn newer tokens without extra trips. This reduces load while still converging quickly.

alex: Good call. Action items: 
- [alex] push synthetic repro harness + raw logs to this thread by EOD.
- [jing] prototype token metadata sketch and rough perf model (qps impact, memory) by Wed.
- [sophie] write canary test and k6 script to run in staging with toggled sequencer lag by Thu.
- [ravi] explore piggybacking token bumps on existing RPCs to avoid separate writes; sync after standup.

prefetch-bot: EvictionReproTests finished. metrics: stale_reads=3/1000000, revalidation p99 +1.8ms.

alex: We'll discuss correctness thresholds in the weekly infra sync. For now prototype token approach seems like the best tradeoff. Thanks all :thumbsup:
